1:1.meaning: The blind king Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya: what did my sons and Pandu's sons do when they gathered to fight on the holy field of Kurukshetra?

1:2.meaning: Sanjaya answers: seeing the Pandava army drawn up for battle, Prince Duryodhana went to his teacher Drona and spoke.

1:3.meaning: Duryodhana says: O teacher, look at this mighty Pandava army, drawn up by your clever pupil, Drupada's son.

1:4.meaning: Here are heroes, great archers, the equals of Bhima and Arjuna in battle: Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada the great warrior.

1:5.meaning: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, the brave king of Kashi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, the best of men.

1:6.meaning: Yudhamanyu and the strong Uttamaujas, Abhimanyu, and Draupadi's sons — all of them great warriors.

1:7.meaning: Now hear about our own chiefs, O best of learned men. I will name the leaders of my army so you know them.

1:8.meaning: Yourself, and Bhishma, Karna, Kripa the winner of battles, Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and Somadatta's son.

1:9.meaning: And many other heroes, skilled with every kind of weapon. They have given up their lives for me.

1:10.meaning: Our army, guarded by Bhishma, is beyond measure; theirs, guarded by Bhima, is small.

1:11.meaning: So hold the positions given to you, all of you. And protect Bhishma above everything.

1:12.meaning: To cheer Duryodhana up, old grandsire Bhishma roared like a lion and blew his conch.

1:13.meaning: Then all at once conches, drums, cymbals and horns sounded, and the noise was tremendous.

1:14.meaning: Then Krishna and Arjuna, standing in their grand chariot yoked with white horses, blew their divine conches.

1:15.meaning: Hrishikesha blew Panchajanya, Arjuna blew Devadatta, and fearsome Bhima blew the great Paundra.

1:16.detail: meaning is names only; carried by anchors
1:16.meaning: Yudhishthira blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew Sughosha and Manipushpaka.

1:17.meaning: The king of Kashi with his fine bow, Shikhandi, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and the unbeaten Satyaki.

1:18.meaning: Drupada, Draupadi's sons, and mighty-armed Abhimanyu blew their conches, each apart.

1:19.meaning: That din tore the hearts of Dhritarashtra's men, echoing through the sky and the earth.

1:20.meaning: Then Arjuna, whose banner bears Hanuman, raised his bow as the weapons began to fly.

1:21.detail: meaning is names only; carried by anchors
1:21.meaning: Arjuna addressed these words to Krishna.

1:22.meaning: O faultless Krishna, drive my chariot between the two armies. Let me see who stands here eager to fight, and with whom I must do battle.

1:23.meaning: I will observe all those gathered here to fight, wishing to serve Duryodhana, the ill-minded son of Dhritarashtra, in battle.

1:24.meaning: Sanjaya said: so addressed by Arjuna, conqueror of sleep, Krishna stationed the splendid chariot between the two armies. It faced Bhishma.

1:25.meaning: And before Bhishma, Drona and all the kings of the earth, Krishna said: O Arjuna, behold these Kurus gathered together.

1:26.meaning: There Arjuna saw fathers and grandfathers. Teachers, uncles, brothers, sons and grandsons — and comrades.

1:27.meaning: Arjuna saw fathers-in-law and friends on both sides — all his kin arrayed for war. Pity overwhelmed him, and he spoke in despair.

1:28.meaning: Arjuna said: seeing these kinsmen come to fight, Krishna, my limbs fail me and my mouth goes dry.

1:29.meaning: My body trembles and my hair stands on end.

1:30.meaning: My great bow slips from my hand, my skin burns, and I cannot even stand steady.

1:31.meaning: My mind reels as if drunk. I see bad omens, Krishna, and no good at all in killing my own kin.

1:32.meaning: I want no victory, Krishna, no kingdom, no pleasures.

1:33.meaning: Of what use is a kingdom to us, Govinda? What use are pleasures, or even life?

1:34.meaning: The very people we want kingdoms and pleasures for stand here ready to die. Teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, uncles, in-laws, grandsons, brothers-in-law, kin.

1:35.meaning: I do not wish to kill these men, though they would kill me — not even to rule the three worlds, let alone this earth.

1:36.meaning: What joy would be ours, Janardana, after killing Dhritarashtra's sons? Killing these criminals, sin alone would cling to us.

1:37.meaning: So we must not kill our kinsmen. How could we ever be happy, Madhava, after killing our own people?

1:38.meaning: Even though these men, blinded by greed, see no evil in wiping out a family or betraying friends —

1:39.meaning: should not we, who DO see the evil in destroying a family, turn back from this sin?

1:40.meaning: When a family dies out, its timeless duties die with it. And when duty dies, lawlessness takes over the whole clan.

1:41.meaning: When lawlessness wins, Krishna, the women of the house go astray, and from that comes the mixing of duties.

1:42.meaning: That mixing drags the family and its destroyers down to hell. The forefathers fall, their offerings of food and water cut off.

1:43.meaning: The destroyers' misdeeds wipe out the timeless duties of ranks and families.

1:44.meaning: And we have heard, Janardana, that men without family duties must live in hell.

1:45.meaning: Alas! We are set to commit a terrible sin, ready to kill our own kin out of greed for a kingdom's pleasures.

1:46.meaning: If Dhritarashtra's sons killed me in battle — weaponless, refusing to fight back — that would be better for me.

1:47.meaning: Sanjaya said: having spoken thus, Arjuna dropped his bow and arrows. He sank into his chariot, his mind drowned in grief.

2:1.meaning: Sanjaya said: to Arjuna, drowned in pity, his eyes full of tears and troubled, Krishna spoke these words.

2:2.meaning: Krishna said: where has this weakness come from, Arjuna, here on the field of battle? It suits no noble man, wins no heaven, and brings only shame.

2:3.meaning: Do not turn coward, Arjuna. It does not suit you. Shake off this petty faint-heartedness and stand up, scorcher of foes.

2:4.meaning: Arjuna said: how can I shoot arrows at Bhishma and Drona in battle, Krishna? Both deserve my worship, destroyer of foes.

2:5.meaning: Better to beg for food in this world than kill these great teachers. Killing them, I would enjoy only blood-stained pleasures.

2:6.meaning: We do not even know which is better for us — victory or defeat. The sons of Dhritarashtra stand before us, and we would not want to live after killing them.

2:7.meaning: My heart is poisoned by pity, and my mind is confused about duty. Tell me plainly what is good. I am your student now — teach me.

2:8.meaning: I see nothing that could drive away this grief. It dries up my senses. Not rule over a rich, unrivaled earth. Not even lordship of the gods.

2:9.meaning: Sanjaya said: having spoken thus to Krishna, Arjuna said, I will not fight — and fell silent.

2:10.meaning: To Arjuna, grieving between the two armies, Krishna spoke these words with a slight smile.

2:11.meaning: You grieve for those who deserve no grief, yet your words sound wise. The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead.

2:12.meaning: Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these kings. And none of us will ever cease to be.

2:13.meaning: As childhood, youth, and old age come to the body, so the self moves on to another body. Steady people are not confused by this.

2:14.meaning: Cold and heat, pleasure and pain come and go with the senses, Arjuna. They are not permanent — bear them.

2:15.meaning: The person these cannot shake — steady in pain and pleasure alike — is fit for deathlessness.

2:16.meaning: The unreal never truly is; the real never ceases to be. Those who see truth perceive both correctly.

2:17.meaning: Know that which fills this whole world to be indestructible. No one can destroy the imperishable.

2:18.meaning: These bodies, belonging to the eternal, indestructible, immeasurable self, must come to an end. So fight, Arjuna.

2:19.meaning: Whoever thinks the self kills, and whoever thinks it is killed — both are wrong. It kills not, and is not killed.

2:20.meaning: It is never born and never dies. Unborn, eternal, ancient — it is not killed when the body is killed.

2:21.meaning: Know the self as indestructible, eternal, unborn, imperishable. Then ask: how could such a person kill — or cause killing?

2:22.meaning: A person drops worn-out clothes and puts on new ones. So the self drops worn-out bodies and enters new ones.

2:23.meaning: Weapons cannot cut it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, wind cannot dry it.

2:24.meaning: It cannot be cut or burned. Not wetted or dried. It is eternal, everywhere, steady, firm, everlasting.

2:25.meaning: It is called unperceived, unthinkable, unchanging. Knowing the self as such, you should not grieve.

2:26.meaning: But even if you think the self is constantly born and constantly dying — even then, you should not grieve.

2:27.meaning: For to one that is born, death is certain; and to one that dies, birth is certain. So for what cannot be avoided, you should not grieve.

2:28.meaning: All beings begin unseen, appear in the middle, and end unseen. What is there to mourn in that?

2:29.meaning: One person sees the self as a wonder. Another speaks of it as a wonder. A third hears of it as a wonder. And even hearing it, no one truly knows it.

2:30.meaning: The self dwelling in every body can never be killed. So grieve for no being.

2:31.meaning: Looking to your own duty as well, you must not waver. For a warrior, nothing is better than a righteous battle.

2:32.meaning: Happy are the warriors who find such a battle come of itself — an open door to heaven.

2:33.meaning: But if you refuse this righteous battle, you abandon duty and honor — and take on sin.

2:34.meaning: All beings will tell of your lasting shame. And for an honored person, shame is worse than death.

2:35.meaning: The great warriors will think you fled from fear. Fallen from their esteem, you will sink low.

2:36.meaning: Your enemies will mock your strength with cruel words. What could hurt more than that?

2:37.meaning: Killed, you win heaven; victorious, you enjoy the earth. So rise up, determined to fight.

2:38.meaning: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same, fight — and you will incur no sin.

2:39.meaning: This wisdom of understanding has been taught to you. Now hear the wisdom of discipline — holding it, you will break the bonds of action.

2:40.meaning: On this path no effort is wasted and no obstacle exists. Even a little of this discipline saves you from great fear.

2:41.meaning: Here there is one firm resolve. The thoughts of the irresolute branch endlessly.

2:42.meaning: The unwise love flowery Vedic phrases. They promise heaven and declare nothing else exists.

2:43.meaning: Full of desires, heaven-bent, promising rebirth as the fruit of rites.

2:44.meaning: Attached to pleasures and power, their minds stolen by such talk — they never reach steady resolve.

2:45.meaning: The Vedas deal with nature's three qualities. Rise above them, Arjuna — beyond opposites, steady, self-possessed.

2:46.meaning: To the knower, all the Vedas are as useful as a water tank in a flooded land.

2:47.meaning: Your right is to action alone, never to its fruits. Never let results be your motive — and never sit idle either.

2:48.meaning: Established in discipline, do your work, dropping attachment. Steadiness in success and failure — that steadiness is discipline.

2:49.meaning: Action done for gain sits far below the discipline of understanding. Take shelter in understanding. The profit-hunters are pitiful.

2:50.meaning: Joined to understanding, one drops both good and bad deeds here. So devote yourself to discipline — skill in action is discipline.

2:51.meaning: The wise join themselves to understanding. They drop the fruits of action. They walk free of rebirth's chains, to the place beyond sorrow.

2:52.meaning: When your understanding crosses past confusion, you will turn indifferent. Indifferent to everything heard — or yet to be heard.

2:53.meaning: Your understanding is confused by hearsay today. When it stands firm and steady in contemplation, you will reach discipline.

2:54.meaning: Arjuna said: what marks the steady-minded, Krishna? How does such a one speak, sit, walk?

2:55.meaning: When one drops all the mind's desires and rests content in the self, by the self — that one is called steady.

2:56.meaning: Unshaken in sorrow. Uninterested in pleasures. Free of craving, fear, and anger. Such a sage is steady.

2:57.meaning: Untied everywhere. Neither thrilled by good fortune nor disgusted by bad. Such understanding is steady.

2:58.meaning: When one pulls the senses back from their objects, as a tortoise pulls in its limbs — understanding holds steady.

2:59.meaning: Sense objects fade for the abstinent — but the taste lingers. Even taste leaves once the highest is seen.

2:60.meaning: The senses are turbulent. They violently carry off the mind — even of a striving wise man.

2:61.meaning: Holding them all in check, sit devoted, with Me as the highest goal. Who masters the senses owns a steady mind.

2:62.meaning: Dwelling on sense objects breeds attachment. From attachment comes desire. From desire, anger.

2:63.meaning: From anger comes confusion. From confusion, memory fails. With reason gone, one is destroyed.

2:64.meaning: But one who moves among sense objects with senses ruled by the self will find peace. Free of likes and dislikes.

2:65.meaning: In peace, all sorrows end; and the peaceful mind soon grows steady.

2:66.meaning: Without self-rule there is no understanding, no contemplation — and without contemplation, where is peace? Without peace, where is happiness?

2:67.meaning: The mind that chases wandering senses loses judgment. As wind carries a boat on water.

2:68.meaning: So, mighty-armed one: hold the senses back from objects on every side. Then understanding stands firm.

2:69.meaning: What is night for all beings is day for the self-controlled; what is day for beings is night for the seer.

2:70.meaning: Waters enter the full, unmoving ocean. So desires enter the sage. He finds peace — not the desirer.

2:71.meaning: Dropping all desires, living free of mine-ness, ego and pride — such a one finds peace.

2:72.meaning: This is the state of oneness with ultimate reality. Reaching it, one is never confused; settled in it even at death, one merges into its peace.

3:1.meaning: Arjuna said: if calm understanding is better than action, Krishna, why do you push me toward this terrible deed?

3:2.meaning: Your words sound double-edged and confuse my mind. Tell me one clear thing by which I can reach the highest good.

3:3.meaning: Krishna said: O faultless one, I have always taught two paths in this world. Understanding for the thinkers. Disciplined action for the doers.

3:4.meaning: No one earns freedom from action by simply avoiding action. And no one reaches perfection by merely giving things up.

3:5.meaning: No one can stay even a moment without acting. Nature forces everyone to act, like it or not.

3:6.meaning: Whoever locks down the senses but keeps dreaming of pleasures is a fraud — a hypocrite.

3:7.meaning: But whoever steers the senses with the mind stands far above. Unattached. Body put to good work.

3:8.meaning: So do your proper work. Action beats inaction — you cannot even keep your body going without it.

3:9.meaning: This world is chained by every act except acts done as offering. So work as an offering, free of clinging.

3:10.meaning: In the beginning the Creator made humans together with sacrifice, and said: grow with this. Let it grant everything you want.

3:11.meaning: Nourish the gods with sacrifice, and the gods will nourish you. Nourishing each other, you will reach the highest good.

3:12.meaning: The gods give you the enjoyments you ask for. Whoever enjoys them without giving back is a thief.

3:13.meaning: Good people who eat what remains after offering are freed from all wrong. The selfish, who cook only for themselves, eat sin.

3:14.meaning: From food come all creatures. From rain comes food. From sacrifice comes rain. And sacrifice comes from action.

3:15.meaning: Know that action comes from the Vedas, and the Vedas from the Imperishable. So the all-seeing Vedas forever turn around sacrifice.

3:16.meaning: Whoever refuses to turn this wheel here — living in sin, slave to the senses — lives a wasted life.

3:17.meaning: But one who delights only in the self, content in the self, pleased with the self — has nothing left to do.

3:18.meaning: Such a person gains nothing by acting and loses nothing by resting. And nobody's help does such a one need.

3:19.meaning: By action alone did Janaka and others reach perfection. Act — if only to hold the world together.

3:20.meaning: Whatever a great person does, others copy. People follow whatever such a one treats as right.

3:21.meaning: There is nothing I must do in all three worlds. Nothing to gain that I have not gained. And yet I keep working.

3:22.meaning: For if I ever stopped working tirelessly, everyone would follow my path to ruin. If I abandoned action, these worlds would collapse, and I would destroy all beings.

3:23.meaning: If I stopped working, people would sink into laziness. Worlds would break. I would corrupt every race and ruin all beings.

3:24.meaning: The ignorant act attached to their deeds. So should the wise act — unattached, to hold the world together.

3:25.meaning: The wise should not shake the minds of the ignorant, who cling to deeds. Working devoutly themselves, let them set everyone to work.

3:26.meaning: The self, blinded by ego, thinks 'I am the doer.' But nature's qualities perform every deed.

3:27.meaning: But one who knows the truth stays unattached. It is only qualities playing among qualities.

3:28.meaning: Those fooled by nature's qualities cling to its workings. The wise must not unsettle such half-knowing, slow minds.

3:29.meaning: Hand all your actions to Me, mind fixed on the self, free of hope and ego. Then fight, your fever gone.

3:30.meaning: Dedicate all your actions to Me, mind anchored in the highest self. Fight free of hope, of mine-ness, of fever.

3:31.meaning: Those who live by this teaching of Mine, full of faith and free of nitpicking — they are freed from the bonds of action.

3:32.meaning: But those who sneer at My teaching and ignore it are senseless, confused in all knowledge, and lost.

3:33.meaning: Even the wise act according to their nature. All beings follow nature — what can repression do?

3:34.meaning: Every sense has its likes and dislikes toward its objects. Never bow to either — both are your enemies on the path.

3:35.meaning: Your own duty, done badly, beats another's duty done well. Death in your own duty is fine; a borrowed path is perilous.

3:36.meaning: Arjuna said: but what drives a person to sin, Krishna, even unwillingly, as if dragged by force?

3:37.meaning: Krishna said: it is desire, it is anger — born of passion, all-devouring, terribly sinful. Know it as the enemy here.

3:38.meaning: As fire is veiled by smoke, a mirror by dust, a baby by the womb — so wisdom is veiled by desire.

3:39.meaning: Wisdom is smothered by this eternal enemy of the wise. Desire burns like fire. It is never satisfied.

3:40.meaning: The senses, the mind and understanding are its home. Through them desire confuses the embodied self, veiling wisdom.

3:41.meaning: So first rein in the senses, Arjuna, then strike down this evil thing that murders wisdom and learning.

3:42.meaning: The senses are great. Greater than the senses is the mind. Greater than the mind is understanding. And greater than understanding is That.

3:43.meaning: Know That which lies beyond understanding. Steady yourself by yourself. And destroy this elusive enemy called desire.

4:1.meaning: Krishna said: this timeless discipline I taught to the sun-god long ago. He taught Manu, and Manu taught Ikshvaku.

4:2.meaning: Passed down this way, kings and sages knew it. But over long time, Arjuna, this discipline faded from the world.

4:3.meaning: That same ancient discipline I teach you today. Because you are my devotee and my friend. And this is the deepest secret.

4:4.meaning: Arjuna said: you were born later, and the sun was born long before. How am I to understand that you taught this first?

4:5.meaning: Krishna said: I have lived through many births, Arjuna, and so have you. I remember them all. You do not.

4:6.meaning: Though I am unborn and undying in my being. Though I am lord of all creatures. I take charge of my own nature. And I am born — by my own power of illusion.

4:7.meaning: Whenever goodness fades, Arjuna, and evil rises up — then I make Myself.

4:8.meaning: Age after age I am born — to guard the good, destroy the wicked, and set goodness firmly back in place.

4:9.meaning: Whoever truly knows My divine birth and work like this leaves the body and is never born again. Such a one comes to Me.

4:10.meaning: Freed from craving, fear, and anger. Filled with Me. Depending on Me. Purified by the fire of wisdom. Many have entered into My being.

4:11.meaning: However people approach Me, I meet them that way. All paths lead to Me in the end, Arjuna.

4:12.meaning: Wanting their actions to pay off, people worship the gods here — because in this human world, results come fast.

4:13.meaning: The fourfold social order I created, matching inborn nature to work. And though I made it, know Me as the changeless non-maker.

4:14.meaning: Actions do not stain Me. I hunger for no fruits of action. Whoever knows Me this way is not chained by deeds.

4:15.meaning: Knowing this, even the ancient seekers of freedom did their work. So you too — act, as the ancients acted in olden times.

4:16.meaning: Even the wise get confused about what action is and what inaction is. I will explain action to you — knowing it, you will escape evil.

4:17.meaning: You must understand action, and forbidden action, and inaction too. The truth about action runs very deep.

4:18.meaning: Whoever sees inaction in action, and action in inaction — that person is wise. Disciplined. Doing every deed fully.

4:19.meaning: The wise call learned the one whose every act is free of selfish desire. Free of planning. Whose deeds are burned up in the fire of wisdom.

4:20.meaning: Dropping clinging to results. Always content. Needing nothing. Such a one does nothing at all — even while acting hard.

4:21.meaning: Expecting nothing. Mind and self controlled. Owning nothing. One incurs no wrong by acting merely to keep the body going.

4:22.meaning: Content with whatever comes on its own. Beyond opposites. Free of envy. Steady in success and failure. Such a one is never chained, however hard one acts.

4:23.meaning: For one free of clinging. Liberated. Mind anchored in wisdom. Acting only as offering. Every deed fully dissolves.

4:24.meaning: The offering is ultimate reality. The offered, into its fire. Ultimate reality is the goal — for one absorbed in it through action.

4:25.meaning: Some worship the gods with offerings. Others offer the act itself into ultimate reality's fire.

4:26.meaning: Others offer hearing and the rest of the senses into the fires of restraint. Others offer sights and sounds into the fires of the senses.

4:27.meaning: Others offer every sense-act into the fire of self-restraint. And every breath. Lit by wisdom.

4:28.meaning: Others offer wealth. Or penance. Or focus, study, wisdom. Ascetics of strict vows.

4:29.meaning: Others, eating little, pour one breath into another, then hold both still — devoted to breath control.

4:30.meaning: All of these know sacrifice, and sacrifice burns away their wrongs.

4:31.meaning: Those who taste the nectar left from sacrifice reach the eternal ultimate reality. This world is not for the non-sacrificer — how then the next?

4:32.meaning: So sacrifices of many kinds lie spread in the Vedas. Know them all born of action — and knowing this, you will be free.

4:33.meaning: The sacrifice of wisdom beats any gift of wealth. Every action is fully contained in wisdom.

4:34.meaning: Learn it by bowing down, by asking, by serving. Those who see truth will teach you wisdom.

4:35.meaning: Learning it, you will never fall into this confusion again. Through it you will see all beings — every one — first in yourself, then in Me.

4:36.meaning: Even if you are the worst sinner alive, you will cross all wrongdoing on the raft of wisdom alone.

4:37.meaning: As a blazing fire turns fuel to ash, so wisdom's fire turns all actions to ash.

4:38.meaning: Nothing purifies in this world like wisdom. In time, the self, perfected in discipline, finds it within.

4:39.meaning: The faithful one, senses restrained, devoted — gains wisdom. Gaining wisdom, one soon reaches supreme peace.

4:40.meaning: The ignorant, the faithless, the doubting self destroys itself. Neither this world nor the next — nor any happiness — belongs to the doubter.

4:41.meaning: Actions do not chain the self-possessed. The one who renounced action through discipline. Whose doubts wisdom destroyed.

4:42.meaning: So cut this doubt born of ignorance with the sword of wisdom. Stand in discipline and rise up to fight.

5:1.meaning: Arjuna said: you praise giving up actions, and also doing them. Tell me plainly which of the two is better.

5:2.meaning: Krishna said: both giving up and doing lead to freedom. But of the two, disciplined doing is the better path.

5:3.meaning: Know that the true renouncer is one with no dislikes and no cravings. Free of opposites, such a one is easily freed from chains.

5:4.meaning: Only children, not wise people, say understanding and disciplined action are different things. Master either one fully and you reap both rewards.

5:5.meaning: The peace that thinkers reach, doers reach too. Whoever sees understanding and action as one — sees truly.

5:6.meaning: Giving up without discipline is hard and painful. But the sage grounded in discipline soon reaches ultimate reality.

5:7.meaning: One whose self is pure. Self controlled. Senses ruled. Who sees the same self in every being. Acts without getting stained.

5:8.meaning: The disciplined knower thinks 'I do nothing at all.' This while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving. Sleeping, breathing, speaking, excreting, grasping. Opening and closing the eyes.

5:9.meaning: Casting off clinging, one who acts as an offering to ultimate reality stays unstained. Like a lotus leaf untouched by water.

5:10.meaning: Devotees act for self-purification alone. With body, mind, understanding — even senses. Dropping all clinging.

5:11.meaning: Dropping results, one gains the highest peace. But the undisciplined, hungry for results, stay chained by desire.

5:12.meaning: The self-ruled self sits at ease in the nine-gated city of the body. Neither acting. Nor causing action.

5:13.meaning: The Lord starts no one's actions, nor anyone's capacity to act, nor links deeds to results. Nature alone does all that.

5:14.meaning: The Lord takes on no one's sin or merit. Wisdom lies covered by ignorance — and so all beings wander confused.

5:15.meaning: But those whose ignorance wisdom destroys — for them, wisdom shines like the sun on the highest truth.

5:16.meaning: Minds fixed on That. Selves merged in That. Devoted to That. That as their final goal. They never return, their wrongs washed away by wisdom.

5:17.meaning: The wise see the same in a learned humble priest, a cow, an elephant, a dog — even a dog-eating outcast.

5:18.meaning: Even here on earth, the steady-minded conquer rebirth. For ultimate reality is flawless and steady. And in it they rest.

5:19.meaning: One who knows ultimate reality, mind steady, undeluded, resting in it. Such a one neither cheers at pleasant things nor mourns unpleasant ones.

5:20.meaning: Detached from outer contacts, one finds the happiness inside the self. Joined to ultimate reality through focus. Unbreakable happiness.

5:21.meaning: Pleasures born of contact are wombs of suffering — they begin and they end. The wise take no delight in them.

5:22.meaning: Whoever can bear, even in this life before death, the surges of desire and anger — that person is disciplined. That person is happy.

5:23.meaning: Happy within. Sporting within. Lit from within. Such a devotee, one with ultimate reality, reaches ultimate peace.

5:24.meaning: Sages whose wrongs have ended. Doubts cut away. Selves ruled. Devoted to every being's welfare. They reach ultimate peace.

5:25.meaning: Ascetics free of desire and anger. Minds ruled. Knowers of the self. Ultimate peace surrounds them — in life and after.

5:26.meaning: The sage shuts out outer contacts. Gaze fixed between the brows. Breath in and out made even, held within the nose.

5:27.meaning: Senses, mind, understanding restrained. Aimed at liberation. Rid of desire, fear, anger. Such a one is forever free.

5:28.meaning: Knowing Me as enjoyer of all sacrifices and penances, great lord of all worlds, friend of all beings — one finds peace.

5:29.meaning: Knowing Me as enjoyer of all sacrifices and penances, great lord of all worlds, friend of all beings — one finds peace.

6:1.meaning: Krishna said: whoever does the work that must be done, wanting no reward — that person is both renouncer and disciplined. Not one who just skips rituals or sits idle.

6:2.meaning: Know this. What they call renunciation is discipline itself. No one becomes disciplined without giving up selfish plans.

6:3.meaning: For a beginner on the path, action is the vehicle. For one who has arrived, stillness becomes the vehicle.

6:4.meaning: When one chases neither sense-objects nor actions. Having dropped every selfish plan. Then one has truly risen.

6:5.meaning: Lift yourself by yourself. Never put yourself down. For your self can be your best friend — and your worst enemy.

6:6.meaning: For one who has conquered the self, the self is a friend. For one who hasn't, the self behaves like an enemy.

6:7.meaning: The self-controlled self stays steady amid cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honor and disgrace.

6:8.meaning: Content with wisdom and experience, unshaken, senses ruled — to such a one, a lump of earth, a stone, and gold weigh the same. That is discipline.

6:9.meaning: Whoever sees alike. Well-wisher, friend, foe, stranger. Mediator, the hateful, kin. Good and wicked alike. Such a one stands tallest of all.

6:10.meaning: Practice alone, in a clean, quiet place. Body and mind controlled. Wanting nothing. Owning nothing.

6:11.meaning: Seat firm, neither too high nor too low, layered with cloth, deerskin and sacred grass —

6:12.meaning: Sitting there. Mind pointed at one thing. Senses and workings stilled. Practice discipline, to purify yourself.

6:13.meaning: Body, head and neck held straight and still. Gaze resting softly between the brows, looking nowhere else.

6:14.meaning: Calm in self. Fearless. Firm in celibacy. Mind restrained and fixed on Me. Sit devoted, with Me as the final goal.

6:15.meaning: Practicing like this constantly, the disciplined mind finds peace — the highest peace, union with Me.

6:16.meaning: This path is not for one who eats too much or fasts too much — not for the oversleeper, not for the insomniac.

6:17.meaning: Be moderate in food and play. Measured in work. Balanced in sleep and waking. Then discipline dissolves all suffering.

6:18.meaning: When the restrained mind settles steady on the self alone. Free of hunger for anything. Then one stands disciplined.

6:19.meaning: A lamp sheltered from wind never flickers. So is the disciplined mind of one absorbed in the self.

6:20.meaning: Where the mind, checked by practice, grows still — where seeing the self by the self, one rejoices in the self —

6:21.meaning: That endless joy lies beyond the senses. Grasped only by understanding. Holding it, one never wavers from truth.

6:22.meaning: Gaining which, no greater gain seems possible. Rooted in which, even the heaviest grief cannot shake one.

6:23.meaning: Know that severance from pain-union as discipline. Practice it with resolve and an undaunted heart.

6:24.meaning: Drop every desire born of imagination, every one. Rein in the sense-herd with the mind on all sides.

6:25.meaning: Step by step, grow quiet — resolve firm, courage up. Fix the mind on the self and think of nothing else.

6:26.meaning: Wherever the fickle, restless mind wanders off — pull it back, every time, and settle it on the self alone.

6:27.meaning: Supreme joy comes to the practitioner. Mind fully calm. Passions cooled. Sins gone. One with ultimate reality.

6:28.meaning: Thus always yoked, one shakes off wrongdoing. Supreme joy is touched with ease. Contact with the ultimate.

6:29.meaning: Seeing the self in all beings. And all beings in the self. Such a seer, steady in discipline, sees everywhere the same.

6:30.meaning: Whoever sees Me in everything. And everything in Me. I am never lost to such a one. Nor is such a one ever lost to Me.

6:31.meaning: Whoever worships Me, dwelling in all beings. Knowing all is one. However such a one lives, one lives in Me.

6:32.meaning: Judge pleasure and pain in all beings by your own measure. That practitioner counts as highest.

6:33.meaning: Arjuna said: this discipline of evenness you teach. I see no stable ground in it. Because the mind is so restless, Krishna.

6:34.meaning: The mind is fickle, turbulent, powerful, stubborn. Holding it, I think, is as hard as holding the wind.

6:35.meaning: Krishna said: no doubt, strong-armed one, the mind is hard to hold and fickle. But it can be held — by practice and detachment.

6:36.meaning: Discipline is hard for the uncontrolled. But the self-controlled can reach it by the right means, striving properly.

6:37.meaning: Arjuna said: one full of faith but uncontrolled. Mind wandering from discipline. Missing perfection. What path does such a one walk, Krishna?

6:38.detail: Arnold omits this verse; Telang-only by construction
6:38.meaning: Fallen from both paths. Shattered like a broken cloud. Does such a one vanish, mighty-armed? Confused on the road to ultimate reality?

6:39.meaning: Please cut this doubt of mine completely, Krishna. No one but You can cut it.

6:40.meaning: Krishna said: neither here nor hereafter does such a one perish. No one who does good ever meets a bad end, dear friend.

6:41.meaning: Fallen from discipline, one reaches the worlds of the good. Dwells there long years. Then is born into a pure, prosperous family.

6:42.meaning: Or one is born into a family of wise practitioners. A birth like that is the hardest thing in this world to get.

6:43.meaning: There one regains the understanding of a former life. And strives again toward perfection.

6:44.meaning: Drawn on by former practice. Even unwilling, one rises above scriptural rules.

6:45.meaning: But the practitioner who strives hard. Cleansed of wrong. Perfected over many births. Reaches the highest goal.

6:46.meaning: Higher than penance-doers, higher than scholars, higher even than ritualists is the practitioner. So become one, Arjuna.

6:47.meaning: And among all practitioners: the one who worships Me with faith. Inmost self merged in Me. That one I hold most devoted.

7:1.meaning: Krishna said: hear how you can know Me fully, beyond all doubt. Fix your mind on Me. Rest in Me. Practice discipline.

7:2.meaning: I will tell you the whole story. Both knowledge and lived experience. Once known, nothing more remains to be known.

7:3.meaning: Among thousands, hardly one strives for perfection. And among those who strive, hardly one knows Me as I truly am.

7:4.meaning: Earth, water, fire, air, space. Mind, understanding, ego. These eight make up My lower nature.

7:5.meaning: But beyond this lower nature sits My higher nature. It is alive, mighty-armed one. And it holds up the whole universe.

7:6.meaning: Know that all beings spring from these two natures. I am the birth and the ending of the entire universe.

7:7.meaning: Nothing stands higher than Me, Arjuna. All this hangs upon Me, like pearls strung on a thread.

7:8.meaning: I am the taste in water. The light in sun and moon. The sacred syllable in the scriptures. Sound in space. Courage in human beings.

7:9.meaning: I am the sweet smell in earth. The glow in fire. The life in all beings. And the discipline in the disciplined.

7:10.meaning: Know Me as the timeless seed of all beings. I am the wisdom of the wise and the splendor of the splendid.

7:11.meaning: I am the strength of the strong, free of craving and passion. And I am right desire, where it honors duty.

7:12.meaning: Calm, restless, or dark — every mood comes from Me. But I am not in them. They are in Me.

7:13.meaning: Fooled by these three moods, the whole world fails to see Me. I stand beyond them, beyond decay.

7:14.meaning: Hard to cross is this divine confusion of Mine. But whoever takes refuge in Me alone crosses beyond it.

7:15.meaning: Wrongdoers never reach Me. Neither the confused, nor the cruel, nor minds stolen by illusion, nor those who choose the demonic path.

7:16.meaning: Four kinds of good people turn to Me. The suffering. The curious. The ambitious. And the wise.

7:17.meaning: Highest among them stands the wise one. Always steady. Devoted to the One alone. I am dear beyond measure to such a one. And such a one is dear to Me.

7:18.meaning: All four are noble. But the wise one, I count as My very self. Such a one rests in Me, the goal beyond which nothing stands.

7:19.meaning: After many births, the wise one reaches Me, seeing the divine in everything. Such a great soul is the hardest thing to find.

7:20.meaning: But those robbed of judgment by cravings chase lesser gods. Following rites that suit their nature.

7:21.meaning: Whatever form any worshipper loves with faith — I make that very faith steady.

7:22.meaning: Armed with that faith, one prays and wins one's wishes. Though every gift truly comes from Me.

7:23.meaning: But small minds win small, passing fruits. Worshippers of lesser gods join their gods. My worshippers reach Me.

7:24.meaning: The unwise think Me, the unseen, to have become merely seen. They miss My highest nature — changeless, beyond compare.

7:25.meaning: Veiled by My mystic power, I am not open to all. This confused world does not know Me — unborn, beyond decay.

7:26.meaning: I know all beings — past, present, and to come. But no one knows Me.

7:27.meaning: Every creature enters this world confused. Blinded by likes and dislikes, by the war of opposites, Arjuna.

7:28.meaning: But people of good deeds, whose wrongs have ended, worship Me with firm resolve. Free of the fog of opposites.

7:29.meaning: Those who strive in Me for freedom from old age and death come to know the ultimate. The inner self. And all action.

7:30.meaning: Those who know Me as Lord of beings, of gods, and of sacrifice. Steady in mind. They know Me even at the hour of death.

8:1.meaning: Arjuna said: what is the ultimate? What is the inner self? What is action? Tell me plainly, best of beings.

8:2.meaning: And what is the Lord of beings? The Lord of gods? How are You sacrifice itself, here in a body? And how do the self-controlled know You at the hour of death?

8:3.meaning: Krishna said: the ultimate is supreme and indestructible. Its dwelling in each person is the inner self. And action means the offering that creates and feeds all things.

8:4.meaning: The Lord of beings is all that perishes. The Lord of gods is the primal person. And the Lord of sacrifice is Myself, here in this body.

8:5.meaning: Whoever leaves the body remembering Me at the last moment enters My being. Of this there is no doubt.

8:6.meaning: Whatever form one remembers at the end, to that one goes — shaped by a lifetime of dwelling on it.

8:7.meaning: So remember Me always — and fight. Mind and understanding fixed on Me, you will surely reach Me.

8:8.meaning: Mind unwavering. Trained by steady practice. One goes to the divine supreme Person.

8:9.meaning: Meditate on the ancient Seer. The ruler. Subtler than the atom. Sustainer of all. Form beyond thought. Bright as the sun. Beyond all darkness.

8:10.meaning: At the hour of departure, steady in devotion. Breath gathered between the brows. One attains that divine Being.

8:11.meaning: The wise call that goal indestructible. Free of desire, the ascetics enter it. Seekers of it live the celibate path.

8:12.meaning: Close every gate of sense. Lock the mind in the heart. Hold the breath steady. Rest in unbroken meditation.

8:13.meaning: Chant the single syllable Om — the eternal ultimate — meditating on Me. Such a one reaches the highest goal.

8:14.meaning: To one always yoked, meditating on Me. Mind undivided. I am easy to reach.

8:15.meaning: Great souls who reach Me never return to this passing life — this house of sorrow.

8:16.meaning: All worlds cycle back — even the highest heaven. But reaching Me, there is no rebirth.

8:17.meaning: Those who know a day of Brahma lasts a thousand ages — and the night as long — truly know day and night.

8:18.meaning: At daybreak, all visible things emerge from the unseen. At nightfall, they dissolve back into it.

8:19.meaning: Again and again this host of beings is born with the day. And helplessly dissolved with the night.

8:20.meaning: But beyond that unseen stands another — eternal, unperceived. Never destroyed when all is destroyed.

8:21.meaning: They call it the indestructible, the highest goal. Reaching it, none return. That is My supreme home.

8:22.meaning: That supreme Person — in whom all beings dwell, who fills all this — is reached by love that wanders nowhere else.

8:23.detail: Arnold omits this verse; Telang-only by construction
8:23.meaning: Now hear the parting times. By one road, the departed never return. By the other, they come back.

8:24.detail: Arnold omits this verse; Telang-only by construction
8:24.meaning: Fire, flame, daylight. The bright fortnight. The six months of the northern sun. Going forth in these, knowers of the ultimate reach the ultimate.

8:25.detail: Arnold omits this verse; Telang-only by construction
8:25.meaning: Smoke, night, the dark fortnight. The six months of the southern sun. The traveler goes to the moonlit world — and returns.

8:26.detail: Arnold omits this verse; Telang-only by construction
8:26.meaning: Bright and dark — these two roads run forever. By one, no return. By the other, return.

8:27.detail: Arnold omits this verse; Telang-only by construction
8:27.meaning: Knowing both roads, no practitioner is confused. So stand in discipline at all times, Arjuna.

8:28.meaning: Knowing all this, one gathers every sacred reward. Scriptures and sacrifices. Disciplines and gifts. Then reaches the highest seat.

9:1.meaning: Krishna said: to you who never carp, I will speak the deepest secret. Knowledge married to experience. Knowing it, you escape all evil.

9:2.meaning: It is the king of sciences, the king of mysteries. It purifies. It lasts forever. It asks nothing against duty. It is seen directly and done with ease.

9:3.meaning: Whoever lacks faith in this truth never reaches Me. Such people sink back into the mortal round.

9:4.meaning: I fill this whole universe in unseen form. All beings live in Me. But I do not live in them.

9:5.meaning: And yet — beings do not live in Me either. See the mystery of My power. I uphold all beings and make all beings. Yet My self rests in none of them.

9:6.meaning: As the mighty wind roams everywhere within space — yet space holds it lightly — so all beings rest in Me.

9:7.meaning: When an age ends, all beings fold back into My nature. When the next begins, I pour them forth again.

9:8.meaning: Guiding My own nature, I create this whole gathering again and again. Helpless before nature's force, they come.

9:9.meaning: But these acts never bind Me. I sit apart, unconcerned, unattached to the doing.

9:10.meaning: Through Me as witness, nature births everything that moves or stands still. And so the universe turns.

9:11.meaning: Fools scorn Me in human form. Blind to My highest nature as great Lord of all beings.

9:12.meaning: Vain their hopes, vain their acts, vain their knowledge. Minds unhinged, they slide toward the demonic way.

9:13.meaning: But great souls take refuge in the divine nature. Knowing Me as the endless source of all beings, they worship with undivided minds.

9:14.meaning: They praise Me without ceasing. They strive, firm in vows. They bow in reverence. Always yoked, they worship.

9:15.meaning: Others worship through the sacrifice of knowledge. Seeing Me as one, as separate, as all-pervading in countless forms.

9:16.meaning: I am the ritual and the prayer. The offering to ancestors and the healing herb. The hymn, the butter, the fire, the gift.

9:17.meaning: I am father, mother, maker, grandsire of this universe. The thing to know. The purifier. The syllable Om. The three scriptures. The goal, keeper, Lord, witness.

9:18.meaning: I send the heat and hold the rains. I am death and deathlessness both. Being and non-being alike, Arjuna.

9:19.meaning: Scholars of the three scriptures drink the sacred draught, sins washed clean. They sacrifice, asking heaven — and win the shining world of the gods.

9:20.meaning: But when the joy runs out and merit is spent, they fall back into the mortal world.

9:21.meaning: Chasers of desires, followers of rites — their fruit is going and coming, coming and going.

9:22.meaning: But those who worship Me alone. Meditating on nothing else, always yoked. I secure what they have and grant what they lack.

9:23.meaning: Even devotees of other gods, worshipping with faith, truly worship Me. Only by the wrong road.

9:24.meaning: For I receive and rule every sacrifice. But they do not know Me truly — so they fall back.

9:25.meaning: God-worshippers reach the gods. Ancestor-worshippers reach the ancestors. Ghost-worshippers reach the ghosts. My worshippers reach Me.

9:26.meaning: Leaf, flower, fruit, water — whatever love offers, I accept from a pure heart.

9:27.meaning: Whatever you do, eat, sacrifice, give, or suffer — lay it all before Me.

9:28.meaning: Then you slip free of the chains of action, fair or foul. Yoked in devotion and renunciation, you reach Me.

9:29.meaning: I am the same to all beings. None hateful, none dear. But lovers who dwell in Me — I dwell in them too.

9:30.meaning: Even a lifelong wrongdoer who turns to Me alone counts as good. Such resolve sets one straight.

9:31.meaning: Such a one soon grows righteous and finds lasting peace. Proclaim it: My devotee never perishes.

9:32.meaning: Even the lowborn, women, merchants, laborers — all who take refuge reach the highest goal.

9:33.meaning: How much more, then, holy priests and royal sages devoted to Me? Landed in this fleeting, painful world — worship Me.

9:34.meaning: Fix your mind on Me. Love Me. Serve Me. Bow to Me. Make Me your highest goal, your deepest practice — and you will surely reach Me.

10:1.meaning: Krishna said: hear once more My finest words. I speak them for your good, because you delight in them.

10:2.meaning: Neither gods nor great sages know My origin. For I am in every way the source of gods and sages alike.

10:3.meaning: Whoever knows Me as unborn. Beginningless. Great Lord of the world. Undeluded, such a mortal is freed from all wrong.

10:4.meaning: Reason, wisdom, clarity, patience, truth, restraint, calm. Joy, sorrow, birth, death, fear, courage.

10:5.meaning: Non-harm, balance, contentment, discipline, generosity, fame, disgrace. All these varied moods of beings come from Me alone.

10:6.meaning: The seven ancient sages and the four Manus. Fathers of all peoples. All were born from My mind, sharing My power.

10:7.meaning: Whoever truly knows these powers and glories of Mine stands in unshakable discipline. Of this there is no doubt.

10:8.meaning: I am the source of all, and all moves through Me. Knowing this, the wise worship Me with love.

10:9.meaning: Minds on Me, lives offered to Me. Teaching each other, speaking of Me always. Content and joyful.

10:10.meaning: To these, always yoked, worshipping with love, I grant the wisdom by which they reach Me.

10:11.meaning: Dwelling in their hearts, out of compassion I destroy. Their darkness-born ignorance. With wisdom's shining lamp.

10:12.meaning: Arjuna said: You are the supreme ultimate, the supreme home, the holiest of the holy.

10:13.meaning: Saints call You the eternal, divine, first god — Narada, Asita, Devala, Vyasa. And You Yourself tell me so.

10:14.meaning: All You tell me I hold true, Krishna. Neither gods nor demons grasp Your manifestation.

10:15.meaning: You alone know Yourself by Yourself. Best of beings. Maker of all. Lord of all. God of gods. Ruler of the universe.

10:16.meaning: So declare fully Your divine glories — by which You stand pervading all these worlds.

10:17.meaning: How shall I know You, ever meditating? In which things should I contemplate You, Lord?

10:18.meaning: Tell again, in full, Your power and glory. I never tire of hearing this nectar.

10:19.meaning: Krishna said: then I will tell You My chief glories. For the full extent has no end.

10:20.meaning: I am the self seated in every heart. I am the beginning, middle, and end of all beings.

10:21.meaning: Among sun-gods, Vishnu. Among lights, the radiant sun. Among storm-gods, Marichi. Among stars, the moon.

10:22.meaning: Among scriptures, the song-scripture. Among gods, Indra. Among senses, the mind. Among beings, awareness.

10:23.meaning: Among storm-powers, Shiva. Among keepers of wealth, Kubera. Among elements, fire. Among peaks, Meru.

10:24.meaning: Among priests, Brihaspati. Among generals, Skanda. Among waters, the ocean.

10:25.meaning: Among sages, Bhrigu. Among words, the single syllable Om. Among rites, silent prayer. Among mountains, the Himalaya.

10:26.meaning: Among trees, the sacred fig. Among seers, Narada. Among musicians of heaven, Chitraratha. Among adepts, Kapila.

10:27.meaning: Among horses, the nectar-born steed. Among elephants, Airavata. Among humans, the king.

10:28.meaning: Among weapons, the thunderbolt. Among cattle, the wish-giver. Among creators, desire. Among serpents, Vasuki.

10:29.meaning: Among serpent-kings, Ananta. Among sea-dwellers, Varuna. Among ancestors, Aryaman. Among rulers, Yama.

10:30.meaning: Among demons, Prahlada. Among reckoners, time. Among beasts, the lion. Among birds, the eagle.

10:31.meaning: Among purifiers, the wind. Among warriors, Rama. Among fishes, the sea-beast. Among rivers, the Ganges.

10:32.meaning: Of all that begins, I am beginning, middle, and end. Among learnings, self-knowledge. Among debaters, fair argument.

10:33.meaning: Among letters, A. Among compounds, the pairing of equals. I am endless time, and the maker facing every way.

10:34.meaning: I am all-seizing death, and the birth of things to come. Among women: fame, fortune, speech, memory, wisdom, courage, patience.

10:35.meaning: Among hymns, the great chant. Among metres, Gayatri. Among months, the harvest month. Among seasons, spring.

10:36.meaning: Among cheats, the dice-game. Among the splendid, splendor. I am victory, resolve, and the goodness of the good.

10:37.meaning: Among clansmen, Krishna. Among archers, Arjuna. Among sages, Vyasa. Among poets, Usanas.

10:38.meaning: Among punishers, the rod. Among strivers, fair policy. Among secrets, silence. Among knowers, wisdom.

10:39.meaning: Whatever seeds all beings — that am I. Nothing moving or still can exist without Me.

10:40.meaning: My glories have no end. What I have told is a fraction only.

10:41.meaning: Wherever you see power, glory, or brilliance — know it as a spark of My splendor.

10:42.meaning: Why know more? With a single fragment of Myself I uphold this entire universe.

11:1.meaning: Arjuna said: the supreme mystery You spoke for my welfare has cleared my confusion.

11:2.meaning: I have heard at length of the birth and passing of beings. And of Your imperishable glory, lotus-eyed one.

11:3.meaning: What You say of Yourself is so. Now I long to see Your divine form, highest Lord.

11:4.meaning: If I can bear the sight, Lord of discipline, show me Your imperishable Self.

11:5.meaning: Krishna said: see My forms by the hundred and thousand. Countless, divine, multicolored.

11:6.meaning: See sun-gods, wind-gods, storm-gods, the twin horsemen. Wonders never seen before.

11:7.meaning: See the whole universe, moving and still, gathered in one within My body. And anything else you wish.

11:8.meaning: But human eyes cannot see Me. I grant you a divine eye. Behold My majestic power.

11:9.meaning: Sanjaya said: so speaking, Hari showed the prince His supreme divine form.

11:10.meaning: Countless mouths and eyes. Wondrous sights within. Celestial ornaments, weapons raised high.

11:11.meaning: Garlands of stars, robes of light, perfumes of heaven. Every wonder, faces in every direction.

11:12.meaning: If a thousand suns burst forth at once, that might match this splendor.

11:13.meaning: There Arjuna saw the whole universe in one — yet divided in countless parts — within the god of gods.

11:14.meaning: Amazed, hair on end, he bowed his head and spoke with folded hands.

11:15.meaning: Arjuna said: I see all gods within Your body. All beings. The creator on His lotus. Sages and serpents.

11:16.meaning: Countless arms, bellies, mouths, eyes everywhere. No end, no middle, no beginning in sight.

11:17.meaning: Crown, mace, discus. A mass of radiance, blinding on every side, blazing like fire and sun.

11:18.meaning: You are the imperishable truth to be known. The highest refuge. Guardian of eternal duty. The timeless being.

11:19.meaning: No beginning, middle, or end. Boundless power. Sun and moon for eyes. A mouth of blazing fire, warming the universe.

11:20.meaning: Earth and sky and every direction are filled by You alone. The three worlds tremble at this terrible wonder.

11:21.meaning: Hosts of gods stream into You. Some pray in fear with folded hands. Sages chant blessings and praise.

11:22.meaning: Storm-gods, sun-gods, circlers, ancestors. Twins, winds, musicians, demons, adepts. All stare amazed.

11:23.meaning: Many mouths, eyes, arms, thighs, feet, bellies, dreadful teeth. All peoples terrified — and I with them.

11:24.meaning: Touching the sky, radiant, many-colored. Jaws agape, eyes ablaze. I shake inside, courage and calm gone.

11:25.meaning: These tusk-ringed mouths glow like doomsday fire. I lose my bearings and my peace. Be gracious, all-pervading Lord.

11:26.meaning: Dhritarashtra's sons with all their kings. Bhishma, Drona, Karna. Our own captains too.

11:27.meaning: All rush into Your dreadful toothed mouths. Some stick, heads crushed, between the teeth.

11:28.meaning: As rivers race to the sea, so these heroes pour into Your blazing mouths.

11:29.meaning: As moths dive into flame, so these multitudes hasten to their ruin.

11:30.meaning: Swallowing all from every side, licking them with flaming tongues. Your splendor fills and scorches the universe.

11:31.meaning: Who are You in this fierce form? Salutations, chief of gods. Be gracious. I must know the primeval one — Your deeds pass understanding.

11:32.meaning: Krishna said: I am Time, destroyer of worlds, now risen to devour. Even without you, these warriors will all cease to be.

11:33.meaning: So rise, win glory, conquer, enjoy the kingdom. They are already slain by Me. Be merely the instrument.

11:34.meaning: Strike Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna — already slain by Me. Do not grieve. Fight. You will conquer.

11:35.meaning: Sanjaya said: hearing this, the trembling crowned one bowed with folded hands. Throat choked, he spoke again.

11:36.meaning: Arjuna said: rightly does the world rejoice in Your glory. Demons flee terrified. Adepts bow down.

11:37.meaning: Why would they not bow to You — greater than the creator, first cause? Infinite Lord, refuge of worlds. Being, non-being, and beyond both.

11:38.meaning: Primal god, ancient person. Highest refuge of this universe. Knower and known and supreme goal. All-pervading, infinite-formed.

11:39.meaning: Wind, death, fire, ocean, moon. Creator and great grandsire both.

11:40.meaning: Salutations a thousand times, again and again. Before, behind, on every side — to You who are all.

11:41.meaning: For calling You 'friend,' 'Krishna,' 'clansman' — light words from ignorance of this greatness —

11:42.meaning: For jests at play, rest, meals, and councils. Alone or before others. Forgive me, imperishable one.

11:43.meaning: Father of all that moves and stands. Greatest teacher. None equals You — how could any surpass?

11:44.meaning: So I bow, prostrate, begging grace. Bear with me as a father his son, a friend his friend, a lover his beloved.

11:45.meaning: Thrilled to see the never-seen, yet trembling — show me again the familiar form, gracious Lord of gods.

11:46.meaning: Crown, mace, discus in hand, as before. Thousand-armed one — return to the four-armed form.

11:47.meaning: Krishna said: out of love I showed this supreme, infinite, primal form — seen by you alone, Arjuna.

11:48.meaning: No scripture, sacrifice, gift, rite, or fierce discipline can show this form. None but you has seen it.

11:49.meaning: Do not fear this terrible form of Mine. Glad-hearted, fearless — see again My familiar shape.

11:50.meaning: Sanjaya said: so speaking, Krishna resumed His own gentle form and comforted the frightened prince.

11:51.meaning: Arjuna said: seeing again this gentle human form, my mind steadies and returns to normal.

11:52.meaning: Krishna said: even gods forever long to see this form you have seen. It is hard won.

11:53.meaning: Not by scriptures, penance, gifts, or rites can I be seen as you have seen Me.

11:54.meaning: But by single-pointed devotion I can be known, seen, and entered truly.

11:55.meaning: Who works for Me, holds Me highest, loves Me, drops attachments, hates no being — such a one reaches Me.

12:1.meaning: Arjuna said: two kinds of worshippers. Those devoted to Your visible form. And those seeking the unseen imperishable. Who knows discipline best?

12:2.meaning: Krishna said: those constantly devoted. Full of highest faith. Minds fixed on Me. I count them most disciplined.

12:3.meaning: But others restrain every sense. Minds steady at all times. Meditating on the indescribable, imperishable, unseen.

12:4.meaning: The all-pervading, unthinkable, changeless, constant. Working for the good of all beings. They too reach Me.

12:5.meaning: Still, the unseen path strains embodied beings sorely. The formless goal comes hard to those with bodies.

12:6.meaning: But those who dedicate every act to Me. Holding Me highest. Worshipping with love for none besides.

12:7.meaning: minds fixed on Me — I swiftly lift them from the ocean of mortal death.

12:8.meaning: Fix your mind on Me alone, your understanding too. In Me you will dwell hereafter. No doubt.

12:9.meaning: If you cannot steady your mind on Me, then reach Me through constant practice of meditation.

12:10.meaning: If even practice defeats you, work for My sake above all. Acting for Me, you will reach perfection.

12:11.meaning: If even that is beyond you, take refuge in devotion to Me. Restrain yourself. Give up every fruit of action.

12:12.meaning: For knowledge beats rote practice. Worship beats knowledge. Giving up results beats worship. And surrender brings peace swiftly.

12:13.meaning: Who hates no being. Friendly, compassionate. Free of ego and possessiveness.

12:14.meaning: Even through joy and sorrow. Forgiving, content, always yoked. Self-ruled, resolute. Mind and heart Mine. Such a one is dear to Me.

12:15.meaning: Who disturbs no world, nor is disturbed by any. Free of excitement, anger, fear, and worry — such a one is dear to Me.

12:16.meaning: Unconcerned with outcomes. Pure, efficient, neutral, untroubled. Surrendering every selfish act. Such a one is dear to Me.

12:17.meaning: No craving, no aversion. No grief, no greed. Abandoning likes and dislikes alike — such a one is dear to Me.

12:18.meaning: Same toward friend and foe, honor and disgrace. Same in heat and cold, pleasure and pain. Free of clinging.

12:19.meaning: To whom praise and blame sound alike. Quiet, content with whatever comes, homeless, steady-minded, full of devotion — such a one is dear to Me.

12:20.meaning: But devotees who hold Me highest. And drink this immortal teaching with faith. They are supremely dear to Me.

13:1.meaning: Krishna said: this body is the field. Whoever knows it is the knower of the field.

13:2.meaning: And know Me as the knower in every field. Knowing field and knower — that is true knowledge.

13:3.meaning: Hear briefly what the field is, what it is like, its changes, its source. Who the knower is, and his powers.

13:4.detail: Arnold omits this verse; Telang-only by construction
13:4.meaning: Sages have sung this in many hymns, distinctly. In reasoned texts that reveal the ultimate.

13:5.meaning: The five elements, ego, intellect, the unseen. Ten senses plus mind. Five sense-objects.

13:6.meaning: Desire, hatred, pleasure, pain. Body, awareness, resolve. This, in brief, is the field with all its changes.

13:7.meaning: Humility, honesty, harmlessness. Patience, honor, reverence for teachers. Purity, steadiness, self-rule.

13:8.meaning: Freedom from sense slavery. Freedom from ego. Seeing the pain in birth, death, age, and disease.

13:9.meaning: No clinging to children, spouse, or home. Even-minded through welcome and unwelcome alike.

13:10.meaning: Unswerving devotion to Me alone. Love of solitude. Hunger for self-knowledge.

13:11.meaning: Constancy in truth-seeking. Seeing what wisdom aims at. This is knowledge. Its opposite is ignorance.

13:12.meaning: Now hear the goal of knowing. The supreme ultimate. Beginningless. Neither being nor non-being.

13:13.meaning: Hands and feet everywhere. Eyes, heads, faces everywhere. Ears everywhere. Enfolding all.

13:14.meaning: Enjoying every sense, yet senseless. Detached, yet upholding all. Quality-free, yet tasting qualities.

13:15.meaning: Inside all, outside all. Moving and unmoving. Too subtle to grasp. Farther than far, nearer than near.

13:16.meaning: Undivided, yet seemingly divided among beings. To be known as sustainer, devourer, creator.

13:17.meaning: Light of all lights, beyond darkness. Wisdom, its goal, its path — planted in every heart.

13:18.meaning: Field, wisdom, and goal — thus declared in brief. My devotee who grasps this grows fit for oneness with Me.

13:19.meaning: Know this: both nature and spirit are beginningless. And every change and mood is born of nature.

13:20.meaning: Nature drives the body and senses to act. Spirit experiences pleasure and pain.

13:21.meaning: Spirit wedded to nature tastes nature's moods. Clinging to them decides the next womb, high or low.

13:22.meaning: Yet spirit in the body is also witness, approver, supporter, experiencer. Great Lord. Supreme Self.

13:23.meaning: Whoever truly knows spirit, nature, and nature's moods is never reborn. Whatever life one leads.

13:24.meaning: Some see the Self by meditation. Some by philosophy. Some by selfless action.

13:25.meaning: Others only hear the teaching and trust it, devoted. They too cross beyond death.

13:26.meaning: Whatever lives and moves or stands still is born of the field meeting its knower.

13:27.meaning: Who sees the supreme Lord dwelling equally in all beings — undying amid the dying — truly sees.

13:28.meaning: Seeing the Lord the same everywhere harms not the self by the self. Then comes the highest goal.

13:29.meaning: Who sees all acts done by nature alone — and the self as no doer — truly sees.

13:30.meaning: Seeing all separate beings rooted in One. Spreading from One. One becomes the ultimate.

13:31.meaning: The imperishable Self is beginningless. Beyond qualities. Lodged in the body. It neither acts nor stains.

13:32.meaning: All-pervading space stays unstained. So the Self in every body stays unstained.

13:33.meaning: As one sun lights the whole world, the knower lights the entire field.

13:34.meaning: Seeing with wisdom's eye the field-knower divide — and beings freed from nature — one reaches the supreme.

14:1.meaning: Krishna said: again I declare the highest wisdom. Learning it, all sages reached perfection.

14:2.meaning: Rooted in this wisdom, united with My essence. No birth at creation. No pain at dissolution.

14:3.meaning: The great expanse is My womb. I plant the seed. From this union, all beings are born.

14:4.meaning: Whatever forms emerge from any womb — the expanse is mother, and I am the seed-giving father.

14:5.meaning: Clarity, passion, inertia. Nature's three moods. They bind the undying self inside the body.

14:6.meaning: Clarity, pure and luminous, free of stain, binds through joy and wisdom.

14:7.meaning: Passion is thirst — born of craving and clinging. It binds the embodied through endless doing.

14:8.meaning: Inertia is ignorance-born. It deludes every embodied being. It binds through neglect, laziness, and sleep.

14:9.meaning: Clarity pulls toward joy. Passion toward action. Inertia veils wisdom and pulls toward neglect.

14:10.meaning: Each mood rules when the other two recede. Clarity, then passion, then inertia — by turns.

14:11.meaning: When every sense-door shines with understanding. Clarity is on the throne.

14:12.meaning: Greed, drive, restless doing, discontent, craving — these mark the reign of passion.

14:13.meaning: Dimness, inertia, neglect, confusion. These mark the reign of inertia.

14:14.meaning: Dying in clarity, one reaches the pure worlds of the wise.

14:15.meaning: Dying in passion, one is reborn among the driven. Dying in inertia, among the ignorant.

14:16.meaning: Good acts ripen into purity. Passionate acts into pain. Inert acts into darkness.

14:17.meaning: Clarity yields wisdom. Passion yields greed. Inertia yields neglect, confusion, darkness.

14:18.meaning: The clear rise upward. The passionate stay midway. The inert sink down.

14:19.meaning: Who sees moods alone as the doers — and knows what stands beyond moods — enters My essence.

14:20.meaning: Rising past the three moods that build the body, one gains deathlessness — free of birth, age, and sorrow.

14:21.meaning: Arjuna said: what marks one past the moods? How does such a one live? How transcend them?

14:22.meaning: Krishna said: meet clarity, drive, and delusion. Without hatred at their coming. Nor craving at their going.

14:23.meaning: who sits aside, unshaken, steady, watching moods as mere moods —

14:24.meaning: self-contained, same in joy and pain, same toward clod, stone, and gold, steady through praise and blame —

14:25.meaning: Same in honor and disgrace. Same to friend and foe. Abandoning all selfish schemes. Such a one has transcended.

14:26.meaning: And whoever serves Me with undivided love rises past all moods. Fit for oneness with ultimate reality.

14:27.meaning: For I am the home of the ultimate. Of deathless freedom. Eternal duty. Unbroken joy.

15:1.meaning: Krishna said: roots above, branches below. The timeless fig tree. Its leaves are hymns. Who knows it knows all sacred lore.

15:2.meaning: Its branches spread high and low, fed by nature's moods. Sense-objects are its shoots. Down in the human world, action-growing roots spread wide.

15:3.meaning: Neither its form, nor end, nor beginning, nor ground is seen here. So cut this deep-rooted tree with the tough axe of detachment.

15:4.meaning: Then seek the place of no return — resting on the primal being from whom this ancient world-tree grew.

15:5.meaning: The proud-free, delusion-free, attachment-conquered. Constant in self-knowledge. Wanting nothing. Beyond pleasure and pain. They reach the imperishable home, undeluded.

15:6.meaning: Neither sun, nor moon, nor fire lights that highest home of Mine. Going there, none return.

15:7.meaning: A spark of Me becomes the living soul in this mortal world — drawing mind and five senses along.

15:8.meaning: Moving house between bodies, the soul carries its senses along — as wind carries scent from flowers.

15:9.meaning: Through ear, eye, touch, taste, smell, and mind, the soul enjoys the sense-world.

15:10.meaning: The deluded never notice the soul arriving, leaving, or enjoying. Those with wisdom's eyes see.

15:11.meaning: Striving seers perceive the soul within. The unrefined and undiscerning never do — strive as they might.

15:12.meaning: The light in sun, moon, and fire that fills the world — know that glory as Mine.

15:13.meaning: I enter the earth and uphold all life. As the moon, I feed every plant.

15:14.meaning: As digestive fire in every body. Joined with every breath. I cook all four kinds of food.

15:15.detail: Arnold omits this verse; Telang-only by construction
15:15.meaning: I sit in every heart — source of memory, wisdom, and forgetting. I am the meaning of all scriptures, their author, their knower.

15:16.meaning: Two persons walk this world: the perishable many and the imperishable one.

15:17.meaning: Beyond both stands the highest Self — the undying Lord filling three worlds, upholding all.

15:18.meaning: Transcending the perishable. Surpassing even the imperishable. I am famed as the highest Person. In scripture and world.

15:19.meaning: Whoever knows Me thus, undeluded — highest Person — worships Me wholly, knowing all.

15:20.meaning: Thus I have taught the most hidden teaching. Grasp it and all is done; wisdom is won.

16:1.meaning: Krishna said: fearlessness, pure heart. Steady wisdom-seeking. Generosity, restraint, sacrifice. Study, discipline, honesty.

16:2.meaning: Harmlessness, truth, calm anger. Charity, peace, no backbiting. Pity for all beings.

16:3.meaning: No greed, gentleness, modesty, no idleness. Nobility, forgiveness, courage, purity. No cruelty, no conceit. These mark the heaven-born.

16:4.meaning: Show, pride, conceit, anger. Harshness and ignorance. These mark the demon-born.

16:5.meaning: The divine leads outward to freedom. The demonic inward to chains. Do not grieve — you are heaven-born.

16:6.meaning: Two races walk this world: the divine and the demonic. The divine you know. Now hear the demonic.

16:7.meaning: They know neither right action nor restraint. Neither purity, nor honor, nor truth lives in them.

16:8.meaning: The universe, they say, is lawless, lordless, truthless. Lust-begotten and nothing more.

16:9.meaning: Wrecked selves, small minds, cruel deeds. Holding this view, they are born to ruin the world.

16:10.meaning: Insatiable craving, drunk on ego and display. Clutching falsehoods, they pledge themselves to filthy rites.

16:11.meaning: Endless anxieties ending only at death. Pleasure as the highest good. 'This much is everything' — so they decide.

16:12.meaning: Netted in a hundred hopes, enslaved to lust and rage, they hoard wealth unjustly to feed desire.

16:13.meaning: 'I won this today. That wish comes next. This wealth is mine — and that will be too.'

16:14.meaning: 'I killed this foe. I will kill the rest. I am lord, enjoyer, perfect, strong, happy. Highborn. Who compares? I will sacrifice, give, and feast.'

16:15.meaning: Deluded, storm-tossed by schemes, meshed in confusion. Wedded to pleasure. Down they slide into foul hell.

16:16.meaning: Self-worshipping, stubborn, drunk on wealth and pride. Their rites are theater, against every rule.

16:17.meaning: Clutching ego, force, arrogance, lust, and rage — they hate Me in their own flesh and in others'.

16:18.meaning: These cruel, vile, lowest enemies I hurl. Again and again into demonic wombs.

16:19.meaning: Lost in womb after womb, they sink to the vilest state — never reaching Me.

16:20.meaning: Three gates open into this hell, ruinous to the self —

16:21.meaning: lust, anger, and greed. Abandon this triple gate.

16:22.meaning: Freed from these three doors of darkness, one works out one's own rescue — and climbs to the highest goal.

16:23.detail: Arnold omits this verse; Telang-only by construction
16:23.meaning: Who discards scripture and follows craving reaches nothing. Neither perfection, nor joy, nor the goal.

16:24.detail: Arnold omits this verse; Telang-only by construction
16:24.meaning: So let scripture judge what to do and what to shun. Know its rule — then act in this world.

17:1.meaning: Arjuna said: some worship with faith. But ditch scripture's rules. Clarity, passion, or inertia?

17:2.meaning: Krishna said: faith runs threefold, born of one's nature — clear, passionate, or dark. Hear how.

17:3.meaning: Each person's faith mirrors their being. As the faith, so the faithful.

17:4.meaning: The clear worship gods. The passionate worship spirits of power. The dark worship ghosts and ghouls.

17:5.meaning: Fierce self-torture outside scripture. Stuffed with ego, craving, clinging, stubbornness. Know it as demonic resolve.

17:6.meaning: Fools rack the body's frame. And Me within it. Pain mistaken for piety.

17:7.meaning: Food, ritual, discipline, and gifts — each runs threefold too. Hear the divisions.

17:8.meaning: Fresh, nourishing, hearty, sweet. Strengthening, delightful. Food loved by the clear.

17:9.meaning: Bitter, sour, salty, scorching. Pungent, harsh, burning. Food craved by the passionate. Breeding pain and disease.

17:10.meaning: Cold, stale, tasteless, rotten. Impure, leftover. Food loved by the dark.

17:11.meaning: Rite done as duty, by rule, without hunger for results — that ritual is clear.

17:12.meaning: Rite done for rewards and reputation. Know that ritual as passionate.

17:13.meaning: Rite against rule, without food-gifts, hymns, fees, or faith — that ritual is dark.

17:14.meaning: Honoring gods, priests, teachers, sages. Cleanliness, honesty, continence, non-harm — this is bodily discipline.

17:15.meaning: Speech that harms none — true, kind, useful — plus study of scripture: this is vocal discipline.

17:16.meaning: Calm mind, gentle heart, silence, self-rule, pure intent: this is mental discipline.

17:17.meaning: This threefold discipline, done with full faith. Wanting nothing, devoted. Is called clear.

17:18.meaning: Discipline done for respect and applause, unstable and fleeting — is called passionate.

17:19.meaning: Discipline from delusion, self-torture, or meant to destroy another — is called dark.

17:20.meaning: A gift given as duty, to one who cannot repay, at fit place and time, to a fit receiver — is clear.

17:21.meaning: A gift given grudgingly. Expecting returns or rewards. Is passionate.

17:22.meaning: A gift flung at the unworthy, wrong place, wrong time, with contempt — is dark.

17:23.detail: Arnold omits this verse; Telang-only by construction
17:23.meaning: Om, Tat, Sat — the triple name of the ultimate. From it, priests, scriptures, and rites were made of old.

17:24.detail: Arnold omits this verse; Telang-only by construction
17:24.meaning: So all sacred acts begin with Om — rites, gifts, disciplines, by the book.

17:25.detail: Arnold omits this verse; Telang-only by construction
17:25.meaning: Seekers of freedom act without wanting results, closing with Tat — 'that'.

17:26.detail: Arnold omits this verse; Telang-only by construction
17:26.meaning: Sat means what is real and good. Every worthy act is Sat. Steadfastness in rite, discipline, and giving is Sat.

17:27.detail: Arnold omits this verse; Telang-only by construction
17:27.meaning: And every act rooted in That — rite, gift, discipline — is also Sat.

17:28.detail: Arnold omits this verse; Telang-only by construction
17:28.meaning: But whatever is offered, given, or suffered without faith is Asat. Unreal, worthless, here and hereafter.

18:1.meaning: Arjuna said: mighty-armed one, I want the truth about giving up acts and giving up their fruits — distinctly.

18:2.meaning: Krishna said: dropping desire-driven acts, the poets call renunciation. Dropping every fruit, the wise call surrender.

18:3.meaning: Some sages say all action is tainted — abandon it. Others say ritual, charity, and discipline must stay.

18:4.meaning: Hear My verdict on surrender. It runs threefold, best of Bharatas.

18:5.meaning: Ritual, charity, discipline — never abandon these. They must be done. They purify even the wise.

18:6.meaning: Yet do even these without clinging or hunger for results. That is My settled, final word.

18:7.meaning: Refusing required duty is wrong. Quitting it from confusion is dark surrender.

18:8.meaning: Quitting hard duty from fear of hardship earns nothing. That is passionate surrender.

18:9.meaning: Doing required duty detached and fruit-free. Simply because it must be done. That is clear surrender.

18:10.meaning: The clear surrenderer neither hates hard tasks nor clings to easy ones. Doubts gone, wisdom full.

18:11.meaning: No embodied being can quit acting entirely. Who quits the fruits is the true surrenderer.

18:12.meaning: Pleasant, painful, mixed. Triple harvest for the un-surrendered hereafter. Never for the surrendered.

18:13.meaning: Learn the five makers of every act, taught in Sankhya wisdom.

18:14.meaning: The body, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and fate as fifth.

18:15.meaning: Whatever one does — body, speech, or mind, right or wrong — these five cause it.

18:16.meaning: Who sees the spotless Self as the lone doer, dim of mind, sees nothing rightly.

18:17.meaning: Ego gone, heart unstained — even slaying these armies, one slays not, nor is bound.

18:18.meaning: Knowing, known, knower — three spurs to action. Tool, deed, doer — action's triple shape.

18:19.meaning: Wisdom, work, and worker each run threefold by nature's moods. Hear them truly told.

18:20.meaning: Seeing one imperishable being in all separate beings. Undivided in the divided. That is clear wisdom.

18:21.meaning: Seeing only scattered manyness in every being. Separate and apart. That is passionate wisdom.

18:22.meaning: Clinging to one fragment as the whole, reasonless, petty, narrow — that is dark wisdom.

18:23.meaning: Duty done detached, without likes or dislikes. Wanting no fruit. That is clear action.

18:24.meaning: Action straining with craving and ego. Heavy with effort. That is passionate action.

18:25.meaning: Action begun in delusion. Blind to cost, harm, injury, or capacity. That is dark action.

18:26.meaning: Free of clinging and self-talk, brave, energetic, steady in win or loss — that is the clear doer.

18:27.meaning: Greedy for results, grasping, cruel, impure, tossed by joys and sorrows — that is the passionate doer.

18:28.meaning: Slack, vulgar, stubborn, cheating. Spiteful, lazy, gloomy, stalling. That is the dark doer.

18:29.meaning: Now hear wisdom and willpower. Each threefold by nature. Told fully and distinctly.

18:30.meaning: Knowing duty from non-duty, courage from fear, bondage from freedom — that is clear wisdom.

18:31.meaning: Seeing right and wrong, fit and unfit, only crookedly — that is passionate wisdom.

18:32.meaning: Calling wrong right, seeing everything backwards under darkness — that is dark wisdom.

18:33.meaning: The will that holds mind, breath, and senses steady in unbroken focus — that is clear resolve.

18:34.meaning: The will that clutches duty, pleasure, and wealth for their fruits — that is passionate resolve.

18:35.meaning: The will that will not drop sleep, fear, grief, gloom, or folly — that is dark resolve.

18:36.meaning: Now hear the three joys. Where practice turns to delight and pain comes to its end —

18:37.meaning: Poison at first, nectar at last, born of self-knowledge — that joy is clear.
